sections.h2: Who assesses and who bills property tax in Woodbridge?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work: the township Tax Assessor sets value, the township Tax Collection Office bills and takes payment, and the Middlesex County Board of Taxation hears appeals. The county page says plainly that collection happens at the municipal level and the county gets its portion afterward.

Woodbridge Township property tax offices, from the township Tax Assessor and Tax Collector pages and the Middlesex County Tax Board page
OfficeJobWhere and when
Township Tax AssessorValues every parcel, including new and improved buildings, and administers tax appealsMunicipal Building, 1 Main Street, Woodbridge 07095; 732-602-6002
Tax Collection OfficeProperty tax and water or sewer billing and paymentsTown Hall, 1 Main Street, first floor; 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. weekdays, to 6:30 p.m. on Tuesday
Middlesex County Tax BoardCertifies assessments and hears appeals75 Bayard Street, 4th floor, New Brunswick 08901; 732-745-3350; 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. weekdays

The Assessor's page ties the job to state certification rules under N.J.S.A. 54:1-35.25, and the Tax Board serves all 25 municipalities in Middlesex County.

sections.h2: When are Woodbridge property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Payments are due on the first day of February, May, August and November. The Tax Collection Office mails bills each January and July.

The township also bills sewer separately. A township notice on second-half sewer bills gave October 1 as the due date and Friday, October 10 as the last day to pay without penalty, and it warned that the date the township receives your payment counts, not the postmark. Read the stub on your own bill for the current dates.

If a due date falls close to your closing, ask the Tax Collection Office how it treats a payment received a few days late before you rely on a grace period.

sections.h2: How can you pay a Woodbridge tax bill?
sections.html:
The township takes payment five ways, and each has its own cost and cutoff.

  • Online through the Taxpayer Information site: find the property, click Make Payment. An electronic check carries a $1.95 fee, and a credit or debit card costs about 2.95 percent.
  • In person with cash, check or money order at Town Hall, 1 Main Street, first floor.
  • In the drop-off box in front of Town Hall.
  • By mail: make the check payable to Township of Woodbridge and send it to P.O. Box 5004, Woodbridge, NJ 07095.
  • By ACH direct withdrawal, with separate forms for tax and for sewer.

The in-person counter is open late on Tuesday, until 6:30 p.m. A seller paying off a balance before a deed is delivered will usually want a fast route such as online payment or a certified check at the counter.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Woodbridge assessment?
sections.html:
Appeals go to the Middlesex County Board of Taxation. The Board lets you file a petition online through a portal at my.njappeal.com after you create an account. You may upload evidence at filing or as late as seven calendar days before the hearing, by 4:00 p.m.

The Board's deadline for an added or omitted assessment petition is December 1 at 4:15 p.m., and it must be physically received by then, not merely postmarked. If December 1 lands on a weekend or legal holiday, the last day moves to the next business day.

A homeowner whose senior or disabled deduction is denied files Form A-1 with the county board by April 1 following the denial. For an ordinary assessment appeal, call the Tax Board at 732-745-3350 for the deadline tied to your notice. For added or omitted cases the Board says an appraiser whose report is used as evidence must appear to testify.

sections.h2: What property tax relief is available in Woodbridge?
sections.html:
New Jersey offers an annual $250 deduction for owners 65 or older or disabled who have lived in the state at least one year. You must own and occupy the home on October 1 of the pretax year, file on time, and stay within the income limit set by the state.

  • File Form PTD and your proofs with the township assessor or tax collector.
  • File Form PD5 each year by March 1 to keep the deduction.
  • A surviving spouse or civil union partner may keep it if age 55 or older, on the same home.
  • The township's Tax Collector page also carries a veteran property tax deduction form.

The Division of Taxation held a Property Tax Relief Application filing event on November 2, 2026, with evening hours at its Trenton office and four regional offices. That date has passed. Ask the Division or the township for the next filing window.

sections.h2: What should a Woodbridge seller do about tax still owed?
sections.html:
Request a written balance from the Tax Collection Office for your block and lot before you sign a contract. Quarterly billing means a closing in the middle of a quarter can leave a partial period to settle, so ask how the township credits payments received after the due date.

Keep the paid receipts for the last four quarters in the closing folder. If a sewer balance is also open, ask for that figure separately, since sewer is billed on its own schedule. A buyer's closing agent will usually want both numbers in hand.

A seller who disagrees with an assessment can raise it with the Assessor at 732-602-6002 before the house goes on the market.

sections.h2: What is Woodbridge Township like for a seller?
sections.html:
Woodbridge Township is the oldest original township in New Jersey, chartered on June 1, 1669. It covers 24.61 square miles in northern Middlesex County and counted 103,639 people in the 2020 census, the seventh-largest municipality in the state. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 104,802.

The township is made up of unincorporated communities: Avenel, Colonia, Fords, Hopelawn, Iselin, Keasbey, Menlo Park Terrace, Port Reading, Sewaren and Woodbridge proper. Government follows the Faulkner Act mayor and council form, with a nine-member council.

Roads and rail give the township its reach. The New Jersey Turnpike enters at Exit 11, the Garden State Parkway runs through exits 127 to 132, and U.S. 1 and 9 and Routes 27, 35, 184 and 440 cross it. Metropark, Avenel and Woodbridge stations serve NJ Transit, and Metropark also has Amtrak service. Woodbridge Center is the fourth-biggest mall in the state, and the headquarters of Wakefern Food Corporation, owner of ShopRite, is in Keasbey.

Water matters for houses here. About 19 percent of the township lies in FEMA flood hazard areas, with tidal flooding along the Woodbridge River, the Raritan in Keasbey and the Arthur Kill in Sewaren and Port Reading. The Woodbridge Township School District runs 25 schools and enrolled 13,836 students in 2022 to 2023.

For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied value of $433,000, median household income of $108,928, and a mean commute of 32.5 minutes. Owners occupy 66.0 percent of homes.

faqs.q: When is Woodbridge property tax due?
faqs.a: It is due on the first day of February, May, August and November. Bills are mailed each January and July.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Woodbridge property tax in person?
faqs.a: Pay at the Tax Collection Office in Town Hall, 1 Main Street, first floor. It takes cash, check or money order, and is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays and until 6:30 p.m. on Tuesday.

faqs.q: What is the fee to pay Woodbridge taxes online?
faqs.a: An electronic check costs $1.95 and a credit or debit card costs about 2.95 percent. Both are paid through the township's Taxpayer Information site.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Woodbridge property tax appeal?
faqs.a: File it with the Middlesex County Board of Taxation at 75 Bayard Street, 4th floor, New Brunswick, or through its online portal. The Board's phone number is 732-745-3350.

faqs.q: Can I get a property tax deduction as a senior in Woodbridge?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are 65 or older or disabled and meet the residency and income rules. The deduction is $250 a year, filed on Form PTD with the assessor or collector, and Form PD5 renews it each March 1.
